title: Apprenticeship and skills: the unfinished promise
author: Editorial Desk
summary: Training schemes need quality, stipend and a job at the end.
body:
India has a young population and a large skills gap. Several schemes exist: **apprenticeship** under the Apprentices Act, **Skill India** programmes, the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC), and Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs).

## What works

- Apprenticeships with **real work in real firms**.
- Courses linked to **local industry demand**.
- A **stipend** that allows poorer youths to participate.
- **Recognised certificates** that employers trust.

## What does not

- Courses with **no placement**.
- **Outdated equipment** in ITIs.
- **Low-quality private training** providers.
- Using apprentices as cheap labour with no learning.

## BMS view

BMS has asked that skill programmes be **tied to employment**, that apprentices be paid fairly, and that **micro and small enterprises**, which are major employers, be supported to take apprentices. It has welcomed measures that link incentives with first-time employment, as with the ELI scheme.

## A thought from Thengadi Ji

He used to stress that a worker's skill is national capital. Investing in it pays back many times.
